conventions.convention: Exact and approximate outputs are measurable scalar composites on the same declared input law, using the same scalar unit. A measurable solution selection is supplied, not asserted to exist.

Signed numerical mean bias is b_h = θ_h − θ. The exact observable needs a finite first absolute moment; the approximate output needs a finite second moment for the finite-sample MSE and variance bounds.

Finite-sample guarantees concern independent copies with the original output law and externally supplied population bounds. Gaussian interval claims are asymptotic and additionally assume AC and positive output variance; the studentized quotient is zero at zero sample variance.

Fixed-size mode invokes every callback once, including after failures, and never replaces failed draws. Completion conditioning changes the input law when success probability lies strictly between zero and one.
Certified mode uses N = max{1, ceil(V_h/(δ ε_s²))}; N = 1 supplies no sample variance. Execution and operation counts use exact real arithmetic and supplied finite-return sampling contracts.

Sobol indices use a finite product input law and are undefined at zero output variance. Pick-freeze rows use six mutually independent input vectors; the ratio CLT and MCSE interpretation additionally require AC, an L4 output, and positive variance.
The all-zero example uses n ≥ 2 and p ∈ (0,1), with sample variance divided by n − 1. It is a probability-model example, not an empirical observation.

load_bearing.statement: For Y ∈ L1 and Y_h ∈ L2, and n ≥ 1 independent copies of Y_h, E_s[(Ȳ_h,n − θ)²] = σ_h²/n + b_h². If finite nonnegative bounds satisfy |b_h| ≤ B_h and σ_h² ≤ V_h, with ε_b ≥ B_h and ε_s > 0, then P_s(|Ȳ_h,n − θ| > ε_b + ε_s) ≤ V_h/(n ε_s²).

An exact selected solution map is a supplied measurable map S: Θ → X. A real observable is a map J: X → R such that Y := J composed with S is measurable. Supplied measurable numerical composites Y_h = J_h composed with S_h define approximate outputs on the same input law.

Fixed-size mode draws N ≥ 2 independent inputs, invokes the callback exactly once per draw, and returns incomplete if any call fails. Certified mode, with its supplied law and population certificates and admissible numeric inputs, sets N = max{1, ceil(V_h/(δ ε_s²))} and returns the mean, tolerance ε_b + ε_s, failure bound δ, and RMS upper bound sqrt(V_h/N + ε_b²).

published_dependencies.used_for: Sample mean, sample variance with divisor n − 1, and plug-in standard error.
Population variance and covariance definitions throughout the sampling and Sobol arguments.
Transfer of moments and expectations between equal-law outputs on different probability spaces.
Finite-family variance additivity without requiring an infinite IID extension.
MSE expansion, indicator probability bounds, and mean-bias certificates.
Almost-sure sample-variance consistency under a finite second moment.
Gaussian sampling limit under AC and positive finite variance.
Studentization with the stated convention at zero denominators.
CDF convergence at continuity points in the asymptotic coverage argument.
Bounded-indicator arguments converting almost-sure convergence into vanishing exceptional probabilities.
Normal-law scaling and the continuous, atomless standard normal distribution.
Explicit additional assumption carried by the Gaussian and Sobol CLT suppliers.
Independence of callback outputs as measurable functions of independent inputs.
Completion probability and factorization of the completion-conditioned input law.
Mutual independence and common-law conventions in the finite Bernoulli example.
Coordinate averaging, lifts to the full product, and empty-product conventions.
Subset-sum definition of Hoeffding components.
Variance-component normalization and exclusion of zero output variance.
First-order and total-effect numerator expectation identities.
Exact six-vector row sampler, denominator guard, ratio estimators, and formal covariance matrix.
Joint ratio CLT and scaled plug-in covariance convergence under the stated additional hypotheses.

seams_checked.note: Checked the random-velocity-law definition and sensor-pairing lemma against the observable specialization. The identity-state construction uses the supplied Borel law on L2 quotient classes; continuous sensor pairing gives measurability and finite second moments. The consumer preserves the separate measurable-version qualification for strongly measurable Banach states and does not infer IID sampling or pointwise representatives.

The law-shift proposition uses the general measurable-state/scalar-observable interface faithfully and supplies its own Lipschitz, population moment, and bounded-density hypotheses. Its L sqrt(C) ε estimate follows by Hölder and does not claim empirical certification. The other fd-l01 items introduce no additional use of fd-st02.
